\def \articleABSTRACT{Deep learning for radiologic image analysis is a rapidly growing field in biomedical research and is likely to become a standard practice in modern medicine. We used the publicly available NIH ChestX-ray14 dataset, containing 112,120 frontal-view chest X-rays labeled for 14 thoracic pathologies in order to reproduce the 14-pathology extension of CheXNet and built a modified model, DACNet. The reproduced CheXNet model achieved a mean test AUROC of 0.8125, compared with 0.8414 calculated from the 14 per-pathology AUROCs reported in the original article. The modified model, DACNet achieved a mean test AUROC of 0.8474. As a secondary analysis, per-pathology decision thresholds selected only on the validation set produced test macro F1 scores of 0.2813 for the CheXNet reproduction and 0.3414 for DACNet. The original pneumonia-versus-radiologist F1 experiment could not be reproduced because its expert annotations for the 420-image test set are not publicly available.}
